current_evidence: The council's 'Planning application pre-application' page links only 'Local Validation Requirements (April 2025)' at this URL and mentions no newer list or review consultation; the April 2026 items on that page are the supplementary information form and the fee schedules.

issues.detail: All 25 substantive requirements sit under 'Full planning' with the note 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', while the 'Minerals & waste (county)' and 'County own devt (Reg 3)' rows say '(none) - national requirements only'. ESCC's list covers county matters: minerals and waste applications and the County Council's own (Regulation 3) development. Grokbot's own excerpts show this, e.g. 'Waste & Minerals Local Plan Policy WMP 25', 'NPPF Paragraphs 162-168 and WMP24a of the WMLP All minerals and waste planning'. These requirements belong under Minerals & waste and Reg 3.
issues.evidence: Daylight/Sunlight excerpt: '...WMP24a of the WMLP All minerals and waste planning'; Odour excerpt: 'O1 - Odour Assessment Waste & Minerals Local Plan Policy WMP 25'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are garbled or take text from neighbouring cells, and none gives a real 'Types of application that require this information' trigger. Examples: Air Quality ('A3 - Air Quality Report ... A2 - Air Quality Report (cont.) Types of application that require this information Where to look for further guidance'), Landscape and Visual Impact ('Environmental 23 Document title and Details of the Information that will be required determine whether...'), HRA (a URL fragment plus page-number debris), Energy ('show the carbon reduction expected from the proposal.'), Planning Statement ('Where to look for further guidance The Planning Statement will need to be more detailed...') and Odour (a policy reference only).
issues.evidence: app_type_rows trigger_excerpt fields for Air Quality, LVIA, HRA, Energy, Planning Statement, Odour

issues.detail: Two rows are mislabelled. 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' has an excerpt that is a Natural England Agricultural Land Classification map URL run into air-quality text, so it is not a rural-worker requirement; a county M&W list is unlikely to require one. 'Structural Survey' has an excerpt about window and door replacement specifications in the planning statement, which is not a structural survey trigger.
issues.evidence: 'Agricultural Land Classification Map, Natural England ngland.org.uk/publication/1 41047?...proposal on the air quality of the area.'; 'S1 - Structural Survey ... Any application for windows and doors replacements should include specifications...'
issues.grok_comment: The Agricultural row point is valid. However, the 'Structural Survey' row is the genuine S1 – Structural Survey item: in the source PDF the window/door specification text sits in S1's own "Types of application" cell (raw 1a885b8f26), so the label is correct.
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. The Structural Survey label is withdrawn; the Agricultural row error stands.

issues.detail: 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' and 'Agricultural Land Classification / Soils' have the same garbled excerpt, so one item was split into two rows. 'Ecological Survey' and 'Habitats Regulations Assessment' also reuse overlapping text from the same E2 (EcIA) cell.
issues.evidence: Identical trigger_excerpt on both Agricultural rows

issues.detail: Three 'Submission rules' tab items are guidance-document citations with broken URL fragments, not requirements: 'Sussex Air Quality and Emissions Mitigation Guidance for Sussex itydocument.pdf', 'Land Use Planning & Development Control (2017). t/guidance/air-qualityplanning-guidance.pdf' and the IAQM odour guidance reference ('ance/odour-guidance2014.pdf').

The Design and Access Statement is placed under 'Listed building consent' only, because the excerpt quotes the national definition ('must accompany certain applications for planning permission and for listed building consent'). The DAS is a national requirement. ESCC does not normally determine LBC, and the DAS is not listed against the minerals/waste or Reg 3 application types it does determine.
issues.evidence: 'A Design and Access Statement is a concise report which must accompany certain applications for planning permission and for listed building consent.'

issues.detail: The tab captures only 8 items against 'Req. items' = 28. The document uses coded items (A, B1, D1, E1, E2, H1, L1, N1, O1, S1, T1, T3 and Active Travel Plan), and the workbook keeps the requirement names but not the 'Types of application' column. I could not tell whether other coded items were missed, because the PDF could not be read.

summary: Grokbot's link is the council's current April 2025 list, but I could not read the PDF itself because robots.txt blocks automated fetching, so I could not check it for missing requirements. Grokbot's own excerpts show the extraction is poor: county minerals and waste and Reg 3 requirements are filed under 'Full planning', and most triggers are garbled table fragments.

withdrawn_issues.detail: I could not read the source PDF: WebFetch was refused because the site's robots.txt disallows it, and searches found no other official copy. So I could not check for missing requirements against the source. The issues below come from the workbook's own extracted excerpts and from the planning page.
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: This is an auditor limitation, not a workbook error. The April 2025 PDF is captured and readable in raw (1a885b8f26), so the source can be checked.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. This was a note about what my helpers could not read, not a Grokbot error, so it is removed from the issue counts. The council stays on "Still to check by hand".
